lead.title: Brown planthopper egg fluid protein NlOFP1 switches off rice defences
lead.summary: A New Phytologist paper indexed on 4 November shows that NlOFP1, a protein in the oviposition fluid of the brown planthopper, is deposited into rice tissue, helps eggs resist drying and suppresses plant defence. Rice overexpressing it had less lignin and salicylic acid, more cellulose and weaker resistance gene expression, and the protein binds the photosynthetic component OsFeS. Silencing it lowered the insect's fecundity and egg hatching rate, flagging a possible target for pest control. Peer-reviewed; abstract only read, no percentages were given.

notes.label: Plant science
notes.text: Also in the window: OsERF27 and OsPLT4 time rice crown roots, and GmRVE8a delays soybean flowering and maturity.

notes.label: Biotech
notes.text: A lychee pangenome (12 haplotype-resolved accessions, 314 resequenced) and a 961.94 Mb T2T Jacktree genome lead, plus a Basmati blight resistance paper whose abstract was unavailable.

notes.label: Prairies
notes.text: Soybean virus trials in Korea show early infection costs the most yield; relevance to Prairie soybeans is my inference, and no Saskatchewan crop report was found for this window.

plant.title: Brown planthopper egg fluid protein NlOFP1 suppresses rice defences
plant.summary: NlOFP1 is made in the ovarian follicular cells of Nilaparvata lugens and deposited into rice tissue, where it helps eggs resist desiccation and suppresses plant defence. Transgenic rice overexpressing it had less lignin and salicylic acid, more cellulose and weaker resistance gene expression, and the protein interacted with the photosynthetic component OsFeS. Peer-reviewed; abstract only read.

plant.title: OsERF27-OsPLT4 module and ROS balance set the timing of rice crown roots
plant.summary: The AP2/ERF gene OsERF27 is differentially expressed between proximal and distal crown root primordia and is needed for timely proximal root growth, acting upstream of OsPLT4. Loss-of-function mutants showed disturbed ROS patterns and root formation that was sensitised to ROS perturbation. Peer-reviewed rice work; abstract only read.

plant.title: The clock gene GmRVE8a delays flowering and maturity in soybean
plant.summary: A genome-wide association and deep-learning screen of 257 soybean accessions across 14 maturity groups, in two field environments, flagged GmRVE8a, a homolog of Arabidopsis REVEILLE. Knockout accelerated flowering and maturity and overexpression delayed both, a useful handle for adapting soybean to shorter seasons. Peer-reviewed; abstract only read.

plant.title: Rice amino acid transporter OsGAT2 links nitrogen allocation to heading date
plant.summary: Four promoter haplotypes of OsGAT2 were found in diverse germplasm, and low-expression haplotypes headed earlier, had longer grains and lower nitrogen content. Yeast assays showed it transports several amino acids including GABA, and knockout lines flowered earlier while overexpression lines flowered later. Peer-reviewed; abstract only read.

plant.title: Where sodium sits in tomato leaves tracks differences in cell-to-cell transport
plant.summary: In domesticated tomato M82, which excludes sodium, Na+ stayed in the bundle sheath, while salt-including wild relatives accumulated it across the mesophyll. M82 but not Solanum pennellii showed reduced symplastic transport and plasmodesma permeability under salt, and a screen implicated PDLP1. Peer-reviewed; abstract only read.

plant.title: Maize genetic diversity is largely unstructured by human language groups in Mexico
plant.summary: Using genotype data on about 2,000 traditional maize varieties, over 500 human genomes from Mexico and indigenous language maps, the study finds little overall structure, which it reads as effective seed exchange and mixing by farmers. Beyond shared geography, human population structure added little explanatory power. Peer-reviewed; abstract only read.

plant.source: Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry
plant.title: DUFB stabilises GS1;1 to give broad-spectrum disease resistance in rice
plant.summary: Three DUF-domain genes, DUFA, DUFB and DUFC, are induced by Rhizoctonia solani and nitrogen and act redundantly, with mutant and overexpression lines showing resistance to sheath blight, blast and bacterial blight. The proteins protect GS1;1 from ubiquitin-mediated degradation, and GS1;1 protein is lower under high nitrogen, a possible link between fertiliser and susceptibility. Peer-reviewed; abstract only read.

plant.title: A rare T2 RNase in a basal eudicot hints at the origin of self-incompatibility
plant.summary: Researchers identified a class TI T2 RNase and F-box locus in Akebia trifoliata as a candidate S-locus for late-acting self-incompatibility. This subfamily forms a gradient between class I and class III T2 RNases, offering an evolutionary bridge. Evolutionary study in a non-crop species; abstract only read.

plant.source: Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry
plant.title: GmPRLP regulates soybean nodule senescence via ethylene signalling
plant.summary: QTL mapping and resequencing identified GmPRLP as responsive to the rhizobial effectors NopL and NopP. Hairy-root overexpression accelerated nodule senescence while silencing delayed it, through ethylene genes including GmACS7, GmACO and GmERFs. Peer-reviewed; abstract only read.

plant.title: The CsANT1 module coordinates leaf margin lobing and cell proliferation
plant.summary: A Plant Physiology paper indexed on 4 November reports a CsANT1 regulatory module that links leaf margin lobing to cell proliferation. The abstract was not available in the record, so only the title is relied on here and no results are claimed.

biotech.title: Engineering bacterial blight and leaf streak resistance in Basmati rice
biotech.summary: A Plant Biotechnology Journal paper (3 November) uses host-pathogen evolutionary dynamics to engineer resistance to bacterial blight and leaf streak in Basmati rice. The abstract was unavailable in the record, so no efficacy numbers or editing method are reported here.

biotech.title: Transgenic wheat carrying TtDHN3 from Tritipyrum shows drought tolerance
biotech.summary: TtDHN3 was cloned from drought-tolerant Tritipyrum Y1805 and transformed into common wheat 1718 by the coleoptile method. After 24 h of drought the overexpression lines wilted less and had greater root and shoot growth and higher antioxidant enzyme activity than wild type. Peer-reviewed; early lab-stage result, no field data in the abstract.

biotech.title: Hairy root cultures of wild lettuce make more phenolics after methyl jasmonate
biotech.summary: Stable Lactuca serriola hairy roots were induced with Agrobacterium rhizogenes ATCC 15834 and confirmed by PCR for rolC. Methyl jasmonate elicitation reprogrammed phenylpropanoid metabolism to raise phenolic accumulation and antioxidant responses. Peer-reviewed; abstract only read.

biotech.title: A hidden T-DNA-linked inversion explains a puzzling Arabidopsis mutant phenotype
biotech.summary: In Arabidopsis lines lacking mitochondrial malate dehydrogenase and NAD-malic enzyme, mdh1.1 me2 plants were unexpectedly smaller than the triple mutant under short-day, low light. Genome sequencing found a 137 kbp inverted duplication next to the T-DNA, a caution for anyone interpreting insertion mutants. Arabidopsis-only; abstract only read.

biotech.title: Polychrome probe cocktails tell plant cysteine protease isoforms apart
biotech.summary: Mixing E-64-based probes with different fluorophores gives each papain-like protease family and isoform an apparent colour through differing affinities. It separated RD21-like isoforms, and modelling suggests the C-terminal granulin domain shapes substrate selectivity. A methods paper; abstract only read.

biotech.title: A haplotype-resolved lychee pangenome links variation to flowering time
biotech.summary: The team assembled haplotype-resolved genomes for 12 lychee accessions, confirmed the hybrid origin of cultivar Feizixiao, and combined the pangenome with resequencing of 314 accessions to find variants behind agronomic traits including flowering time. Extensive structural and copy number variation was reported. Peer-reviewed; abstract only read.

biotech.title: Telomere-to-telomere genome of the endangered Jacktree maps its centromeres
biotech.summary: The gap-free assembly is 961.94 Mb with an N50 of 78.05 Mb and 36,446 predicted genes. CENH3 ChIP-seq located centromeres on all 12 chromosomes, and chromosome 1 carries a centromere-like domain with ectopic CENH3. Genomic resource for a non-crop species; abstract only read.

biotech.title: Review: transporters that shuttle carbon and nitrogen between mitochondria and plastids
biotech.summary: This review covers mitochondrial and plastid envelope transporters with confirmed substrates and how they coordinate carbon-nitrogen metabolism, flagging major knowledge gaps. It reports no new experiments, so it matters mainly as a map of targets for metabolic engineering.

biotech.title: Review: how plant cis-regulatory elements evolve
biotech.summary: The review summarises principles of regulatory evolution and argues plant models are well placed to test them because of their high genetic diversity. Relevant to promoter and enhancer design for genome editing, but it presents no new data.

biotech.title: Review: receptor-like kinases in drought signalling from root to stomata
biotech.summary: The review organises RLK roles across three scales: sensing at the root-soil interface, long-distance peptide and ROS wave signalling, and stomatal control in leaves. It identifies RLK nodes as candidate targets for drought-resilience breeding. No new experiments; abstract only read.

ag.title: Early infection by soybean viruses causes the worst yield loss in Korean field trials
ag.summary: Field trials of soybean mosaic virus and soybean yellow mottle mosaic virus infection at three growth stages in three genotypes found that early vegetative infection cut yield most, mainly through fewer pods and seeds. Virus was often found in seeds that looked normal, and seed-to-seedling transmission varied by host-virus pair. Peer-reviewed; abstract only read.

ag.source: Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry
ag.title: Early-stage MoEno1-targeting compound shows promise against rice blast
ag.summary: Deleting enolase MoEno1 in Magnaporthe oryzae impaired growth, melanin and pathogenicity. Screening plus optimisation of isobavachalcone gave 59 derivatives, and II-24 showed in planta efficacy, low phytotoxicity and extra activity with tebuconazole. This is an early lead from the lab, not a product.

ag.source: Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry
ag.title: Review: biodegradable iron chelates for soybean iron deficiency chlorosis
ag.summary: The review covers 3-hydroxy-4-pyridinone iron chelates and nano-delivery systems for iron chlorosis in calcareous, alkaline soils, noting they raise iron bioavailability without evidence of persistence in leaching water. Relevant to Prairie soybean acreage on high-pH soils, though that link is my inference, not the review's.

ag.source: Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry
ag.title: Cytochrome P450 enzymes drive natural florpyrauxifen-benzyl resistance in barnyardgrass
ag.summary: A biotype never exposed to the herbicide had a resistance factor of 3.80, falling to 1.49 with a P450 inhibitor, and the factor rose from 2.37 at 25/20 C to 5.22 at 35/30 C. CYP71Z-like, CYP704C-like and CYP81A-like genes are candidates that still need functional validation.

ag.source: Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry
ag.title: Continuous cropping hurts cassava more than drought in a pot experiment
ag.summary: In a 2 x 2 x 3 factorial pot trial, continuous cropping raised rhizosphere organic acids, lowered pH and cut bacterial diversity more than drought did. Roots mounted jasmonic and salicylic acid defences at a growth and yield cost. Pot study, not field.

ag.source: Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry
ag.title: CSP10 helps fall armyworm resist chlorantraniliprole
ag.summary: CSP10 was upregulated in a resistant Spodoptera frugiperda strain, and RNAi silencing raised larval susceptibility. Binding assays and docking showed it binds the insecticide, with Phe6, Ile17, Tyr21, Val25 and Phe38 as key residues.

ag.source: Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry
ag.title: Carboxylesterase AgBe10 detoxifies abamectin in the soybean aphid
ag.summary: Of 26 AgCCE genes found in Aphis glycines, AgBe10 was most induced by sublethal abamectin, and RNAi silencing raised aphid mortality. Recombinant AgBe10 depleted abamectin in vitro, pointing to metabolic adaptation.

ag.title: Meta-analysis: nano and slow-release antifungals beat plain ones against Colletotrichum in the lab
ag.summary: Across 33 studies and 266 effect sizes, formulated products had a pooled lnRR of 0.42 (95% CI 0.22 to 0.63), a ratio of means of 1.52, with very high heterogeneity (I<sup>2</sup> 93.9%). Only one field trial existed and prediction intervals included zero, so field benefit is unproven.

ag.title: China's soil-pest insecticide registrations show persistent concentration in a few actives
ag.summary: Analysis of 1,513 products approved 2005 to 2025 found a shift from AChE inhibitors toward nAChR-acting insecticides and more mixture products, yet the top 3 actives held 50% to 87% of annual shares. It does not measure real use or resistance.

ag.source: Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry
ag.title: Cyclodextrin hydrogel cuts glyphosate spray drift in wind tunnel tests
ag.summary: At 4 m from the nozzle, drift was 55.7% lower than glyphosate solution and 36.6% lower than a commercial formulation. It stayed effective on barnyardgrass and was safe for glyphosate-resistant cotton. Lab and wind tunnel only.

methods: Last issue was 2026-11-04, so the window is 3 to 4 November 2026 with PubMed entry dates of 4 November; each item's date is the publication date in its PubMed record. Web page fetching and general news search returned nothing dated in this window (latest Saskatchewan report found was from September), so all items come from PubMed abstracts and no company or news items could be verified. Source pages were not opened; only abstracts were read, and two items had no abstract, so nothing beyond the title is claimed. Reviews, Arabidopsis-only and early lab-stage results are flagged. Items from earlier briefings (for example FtMYB15, ZmPHO2, the penoxsulam barnyardgrass paper) were skipped.
